newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks top 5,000 SMI in fourth record close.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks top 5,000 SMI in fourth record close.

text.p: Swiss shares powered ahead on Monday to end above the psycologically important level of 5,000 points in the blue chip Swiss Market Index (SMI), posting the fourth record close in as many days.
Index heavyweights Novartis, Nestle, Roche and Swiss Re were among the biggest winners of the day and helped the whole market, dealers said.
Other reasons for the rise were the strong performance of Wall Street, a favourable interest rate environment and derivatives-linked buying.
SMI closed higher by 76.1 points or 1.54 percent at 5,029.6. The index earlier hit an all-time high at 5,041.5.
All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) ended up 43.09 points or 1.38 percent at 3,170.56.
Volume was heavy with the total value of shares traded on the bourse standing at 2.55 billion francs.
One trader said the fact that the London bourse was closed today did not have any effect on Swiss shares.
Further development was seen depending mainly on Wall Street.
Novartis registered shares added 32 francs or 1.62 percent to close at 2,002, passing the level of 2,000 francs for the first time.
Nestle climbed 36 francs to 1,842 ahead of Tuesday's release of first quarter results for 1997.
Swiss Re gained 45 francs to 1,800, profiting from last week's positive 1996 figures.
Wintertur were up 16 at 1,097, following Swiss Re. Winterthur's results are expected on May 14.
CS Group added five francs to 172.25 francs.
UBS edged up one franc to 1,408. UBS declined comment on a report suggesting it might buy asset manager Scudder, but a spokeswoman repeated UBS's stated interest in an acquisition in the U.S.
Clariant, which today payed out a dividend of 10 francs on its shares, lost one franc to 847.
